clue.text: Put up the shutters with union agreement

definitions.meaning: literally a shop that has been shut for the day, its shutters pulled down
an arrangement by which a trade union requires every worker in a firm to be a member

explanation.surface: A business shuts down after striking a deal with the workers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a store that has been locked up; in industrial relations it is the deal making union membership compulsory.

clue.text: He. takes one pound after another

annotationWithheld.why: He takes one pound after another (6): LIONEL needs L, I, ONE, L, which only comes out by using 'one pound' twice (LI and ONE+L), so a phrase does two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: He. takes one pound after another

clue.text: Fed up-as date is wrong put it back inside

indicators.note: inside places the turned word within the rearranged letters
wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged
put back means the word it is turned round to read the other way

explanation.surface: Someone sick of things sees a date is wrong and pushes it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the letters of 'as date', 'put it back' turns 'it' round, and 'inside' sets the turned pair within the rearranged six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiated means filled to excess, and fed up means sated or sick of something.

clue.text: Nullifying the small-arms ammunition misused in defence

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the other word
misused suggests the letters are put to wrong use, so they are rearranged

parts.note: SAA is the military abbreviation for small-arms ammunition

explanation.surface: Bullets are being wasted in a military defence that comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: SAA is an old army abbreviation; 'misused' jumbles it and 'in' places the result within the word 'defence' as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeasance is the legal act of rendering a deed or contract void, an annulment.

clue.text: Male celebrity, eats a hundred in place of nine

parts.note: HE is the male pronoun

indicators.note: eats has one word swallowing another, taking the letter in

parts.note: a lion is a celebrated person, a social star
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A famous man devours a hundred of something in place of nine.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine are the Muses, whose home in Greek myth was Mount Helicon; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Helicon in Greece was sacred to the nine Muses, so it is their home.

clue.text: Confined to this house-that is the top flat

definitions.text: to this house-that is the top flat
definitions.meaning: the word placed before house makes a name for an apartment on a building's roof

explanation.surface: Someone is confined to a top-floor flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half asks for a word which, with 'house' added, names a top-floor flat: put it before HOUSE and you have the luxury rooftop apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pent means shut in, and joined to house it names a flat on top of a tall building.

clue.text: Unusual danger, raising top-class flower

indicators.note: unusual tells us these letters appear in an uncommon order and must be sorted
raising, in a down clue, lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with the letter I for the figure one

explanation.surface: A rare danger is in growing a prize-winning flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges DANGER as GARDEN; 'raising' turns AI (A1, first-rate) upwards to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is a shrub with fragrant white blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Where Sir Richard lay, having money, in blooming health

parts.note: Tennyson's The Revenge opens 'At Flores in the Azores Sir Richard Grenville lay'
a cent is a coin, a small piece of money

explanation.surface: A knight lay somewhere with cash, glowing with health.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Richard Grenville anchored at Flores in the Azores before his last fight, as Tennyson's poem tells.
explanation.definitionFit: Florescent means flowering, in full bloom, hence flourishing.

clue.text: Necessitate directions to follower

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
a tail is someone who follows a suspect closely

explanation.surface: Someone must give directions to a person following them.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to make it necessary as a consequence, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Sounds as if it might impede this important statement

definitions.text: Sounds as if it might impede this important statement

parts.words: Sounds as if it might impede this important statement
parts.note: a word for a long, weighty pronouncement that also names a lot of food held in the mouth, which would stop anyone speaking clearly

explanation.surface: A speaker worries that something will get in the way of a grand announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a big, impressive utterance (as in 'you said a ...') and a full load of food in the mouth, which would naturally muffle speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A long or weighty pronouncement is jokingly called this, and the same word names enough food to fill the mouth and block talk.

clue.text: He forces his way in with a terribly tired run

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An exhausted runner barges his way into somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters a place uninvited or by force is an interloper, so the description fits.

clue.text: Fool about with sale-item

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a lot is an item offered at an auction

explanation.surface: Someone foolish mucks about with something bought in a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Dragoon to gallop round, rating one point

indicators.note: round puts the first word around the letters that follow

parts.note: to career is to rush along at full speed
AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
I is the Roman numeral one
N is the compass point north

explanation.surface: A cavalryman gallops around, judging a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to gallop' is a verb phrase, so its synonym is the verb career; 'round' wraps it about the rating, one and point.
explanation.definitionFit: A carabineer was a soldier armed with a carbine, a kind of cavalryman like a dragoon.

clue.text: Stores Sections on the road betray battle-lines

parts.note: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police
a front is the line where opposing armies meet

explanation.surface: Parts of shops by the street are said to give away military positions.
explanation.definitionFit: The street-facing windows and entrances of shops are the parts of the stores that face the road.

clue.text: Showy trick by youth worker

annotationWithheld.why: Showy trick by youth worker (10): the wordplay gives FLAMBOYANT (FLAM trick + BOY youth + ANT worker, def Showy), but the filed answer is the model's FLAGELLANT and the correction is refused because the paper's grid prints BRIDGECLUE (E) at the crossing with 20-across; needs the grid fixed.

clue.text: Apparently unsound interpretation in Berks

definitions.meaning: an interpretation, the way a text or event is understood, which here seems unsound because the spelling suggests a different sound
the county town of Berkshire, abbreviated Berks, an English county west of London

explanation.surface: A dubious explanation is given somewhere in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The town in Berkshire (an English county west of London) is said RED-ing though spelt like the word for an interpretation, hence 'apparently unsound'.
explanation.definitionFit: An interpretation of a text or situation is a reading, and Reading is the big town in Berkshire.

clue.text: Stock-jobbing in Greece I tucked into a scrambled egg

indicators.note: tucked into puts the Greek letter inside the other letters
scrambled, like eggs in a pan, means these letters are mixed up

parts.note: iota is the Greek letter for I

explanation.surface: Share dealing in Greece, where I tuck into scrambled egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Greece I' is the letter I as the Greeks write it; 'scrambled' jumbles 'egg' and 'tucked into' puts the Greek letter inside A plus that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Agiotage is speculation in stocks and currency, which is what stock-jobbing means.

clue.text: Legal sanction for island appointment

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: An island appointment is made with legal approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official authority or command, legal permission to act.

clue.text: Is it used to sweeten rare mead concoction ?

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sweetener goes into an unusual honey drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a brown cane sugar, which people add to sweeten food and drink.

clue.text: It ends debate in the vicinity about, old city

indicators.note: about has the first word go around the city

parts.note: close means near, in the vicinity
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Somewhere near an ancient city, a discussion ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Closure is the British parliamentary motion that cuts off a debate; 'about' has the word for near wrap the old city.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament a closure motion stops further discussion and forces a vote.

clue.text: One's food will do Mr A. N. Other no good, they say

definitions.text: One's food will do Mr A. N. Other no good, they say

parts.words: One's food will do Mr A. N. Other no good, they say
parts.note: alludes to the proverb that what is one man's diet is another man's poison

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their own dinner would harm somebody else.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'One man's ... is another man's poison'; Mr A. N. Other is the stock name for an unnamed person, so 'another man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names this food as what suits one person yet poisons another.

clue.text: Stick to classical present

parts.note: ad is Latin, the classical language, for to
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone sticks to a classical gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick to' wants to be the definition; 'to classical' gives Latin AD, leaving 'Stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stick fast, a synonym.

clue.text: Seine factories building broadcast systems

parts.note: a seine is a large fishing net
works is another word for factories or industrial plants

explanation.surface: Factories along the Seine are building broadcasting equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Seine looks like the Paris river, but here it is a kind of fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting chains of linked radio or television stations are called this.

clue.text: Here is gold, about left centre

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: centre takes the middle letters of the word left

explanation.surface: Gold is found here, somewhere round the left of centre.
explanation.walkthrough: A reef is a gold-bearing vein of rock, as in the Witwatersrand Reef of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners call a gold-bearing lode a reef, so it is where the gold lies.

clue.text: Spenser's heroine graduated to Edward, no less

parts.note: Una is the heroine of Book I of Spenser's Faerie Queene
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate's degree
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A poet's heroine graduates and moves on to Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undiminished, not reduced in force at all, carries on with no less vigour.

clue.text: Guarantee reserve for contract

definitions.meaning: to pledge or bind oneself by promise
to book a seat or room in advance
to hire someone, enter an agreement with them

explanation.surface: A deal is backed by a guarantee and some money held back.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers pledging oneself, booking in advance and hiring, so all three senses fit.

clue.text: Commercial type opposed to customary methods ?

definitions.text: Commercial type opposed to customary methods ?

parts.words: Commercial type opposed to customary methods ?
parts.note: reads as a rebel businessman, but customary is customs duties: one who wants commerce without tariffs

explanation.surface: A businessman rejects the traditional way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customary' seems to mean traditional; it puns on customs, the duties levied on imports.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate of commerce without tariffs or customs duties is opposed to taxing imports.
